contexts.text: A ram = the things of charity.
The rams, etc. in the sacrifices, = lower celestial and spiritual things.
A ram, etc. () = the celestial things of the Church. AC 1823.
A ram = the representatives of spiritual celestial things. Explained.
Spiritual good was represented by the sacrifice of a ram.
The ram seen behind them, held in a thicket by the horns, which was offered for a burnt-offering () = those of the human race who are of the Lord's Spiritual Church. AC 2807:2. AC 2830, Explained.
That a ram, here, = the Lord's Divine Spiritual, and consequently the Spiritual with man; or, what is the same, the spiritual of the human race. Illustrated. AC 2830:4.
The ram (in ) = the Spiritual Church. AC 2832:14.
In  it treats of spiritual good after regeneration; and its Celestial Spiritual is described by the mountains leaping like rams ().
Rams sons of Bashan () = celestial spiritual things.
Incense of rams () = the spiritual things which are of faith.
Rams of Nebaioth () = Divine spiritual things. ( = spiritual truth. AC 3268:2.) ( = the goods of innocence and of charity in the internal man. AC 10042:9.)
Abraham took the ram () = the deliverance of the spiritual by the Lord's Divine Human.
The rams of thy flock have I not eaten () = that of the truth of good He had taken nothing. As sheep = goods; rams = the truths of good.
Twenty rams () = Divine truths.
Skins of red rams () = external truths which are from good... Rams = spiritual things which are of truth; and red = good. AC 9631.
The ram for a burnt-offering () = the purification of good from evils, in the internal man.
Two entire rams () = the purification of the spiritual or internal man; (for) a ram = the Internal of man; thus his Spiritual. AC 9990:2.
The filling of the hand was effected through the second ram, which is therefore called the ram of fillings (). Described.
Thou shalt take one ram () = the good of innocence in the internal man; (for) a ram = the good of innocence and of charity in the internal man. AC 10042:9, Explained, Illustrated.
Earns () = the goods of charity.
Rams, here () = the like as sheep; for rams are their males.
The sacrifices from the ram () = the purification of the internal man, and the implantation of the good of innocence there.
Thou shalt slay the ram () = preparation for the purification of the internal man.
Thou shalt cut the ram into pieces () = the interior things to be distinctly ordinated. A ram = the good of innocence and of charity in the internal man...

Thou shalt burn on the altar with the whole ram () = the internal of the Lord's Divine Human united to the Divine good of His Divine love... A ram = the Internal with man; thus, in the supreme, the internal of the Lord's Divine Human.
Thou shalt take the second ram () = the following state, which is of the Divine truth proceeding from the Lord's Divine good in the Heavens. AC 10060:end.

It is the ram of fillings () = the Divine power... in the Heavens through Divine truth from Divine good... The ram, being the male of the sheep, = the good of charity and of innocence in the internal man; and, in the supreme sense, the same in the Internal of the Lord's Human. AC 10088.
A lamb = the inmost good of innocence; a ram, the interior or middle good of innocence... AC 10137:10. AE 314:6. AE 314:8.
A ram, and sheep, = those in charity.
The rams of Nebaioth which shall minister = truths which derive their life from spiritual affection. ( = all spiritual goods external and internal. AE 391:9.)
The ram, in  = the good of charity and the derivative faith. ( = those in truths of doctrine because in the good of life. AE 734:25.) AE 817:14.
Rams () = spiritual goods.
Rams = internal goods.
Rams = the goods of charity.
To trample on the ram () = to completely destroy charity.
The ram, from the correspondence, = the natural man as to the good of charity.
The spiritual goods and truths in which are the Angels of the Middle Heaven, are signified by the rams (in the sacrifices).
